You want to move mezzaria.it from WooCommerce to Shopify. This document shows what we found on the current site, two ways to rebuild it (keep the current look with improvements, or a full redesign), how your data and Google rankings are protected, and the cost. All prices include our Black Friday · Cyber Monday offer.

1

Why LitOS

One teamLitOS and LitExtension are part of the same company, LitGroup. The people moving your data and the people building your store work together, so your data is mapped to how your theme displays it, in the admin and on the storefront.
2

What we found on the current site

AreaWhat we see todayWhat we'd do
Homepage salesNo products, photos, prices or bestsellers. Only one "Acquista i nostri prodotti" button and a few text links; buyers have to go to the Shop themselves.A featured products section on the homepage (§2.1)
HeroText about the farm, with no direct path to the productsA clear button or link to a collection
AnimationStatic page for a brand that tells a farm storySubtle scroll animations on images and sections
FooterCompany details, social links, contacts and policy links mixed togetherClear columns: shop, customer service, contacts, legal
Shop pageShipping terms sit in the text and the sidebar (§2.2)One separate section with the key information
Product pagePrice, button and shipping note only (§2.3)Delivery estimate, trust points and payment methods next to the button
MobileLong text blocks, menu and cart take a lot of space (§2.4)Improved layout and spacing on mobile
TranslateA "Translate »" widget with 6 languages, but clicking it doesn't workSet up a translation app if you want it (§6, question 2)

2.1 Homepage

The homepage is where most visitors arrive, but today it sells nothing directly. Showing a few products with photo, price and "Aggiungi al carrello" right on the homepage is the biggest single improvement for sales.

2.2 Shop page

TodayThe shipping information (Europe, UK, Switzerland; free shipping in Italy from €79 or with a bag-in-box of olive oil) appears twice, in different words. We'd put it in one clear section so customers see it at a glance.

2.3 Product page

TodayThe current product page: price, shipping note and add-to-cart button, with a lot of empty space under them.

Mock-upThis is a mock-up we made to show the idea, not your live site. Look at the area under the button: delivery estimate, organic farming and payment methods, so the customer has every answer before buying. Final text and details come from you.

2.4 Mobile

TodayThe open mobile menu: the cart sits as a separate row at the bottom. We'd keep the cart and search in the header, always visible.

TodayOn mobile, long text blocks push the products far down. We'd shorten the blocks and bring products and buttons higher.

4

Your data, customers and Google rankings

Your concernHow it's handled
Google rankingsLitExtension's 301 redirect option sends every old product and category URL to its new page. It's a paid option when you buy the migration; we recommend it, otherwise these redirects are made by hand. For pages, blog posts, SEO titles and the new sitemap, we give you a step-by-step guide. Some movement in rankings in the first weeks is normal.
Orders during the moveYour current site stays live until you switch the domain. Just before launch, LitExtension moves the orders, customers and products added in the meantime.
Wrong or missing dataWe check the migrated data in the admin and on the storefront, and work with LitExtension to correct anything that's wrong or missing.
Customer loginsPasswords can't be moved to Shopify. Customers sign in with their email and a one-time code, with no password reset.
